description: Audit of released Sigma workbook-as-code features against documented ThoughtSpot TML semantics. A target is emitted only where the source artifact carries equivalent intent; unrelated Sigma capabilities remain explicit gaps rather than invented dashboard behavior.

rows.notes: Each ThoughtSpot tab becomes metadata-only page metadata and one authoritative layout Page block. Multi-tab workbooks receive an in-canvas auto navigation element on every content page.
Known client-state visibility, title visibility, and placement values map to published Sigma legend fields; unknown settings are not guessed.

Answer TML documents axis_configs only as axis column assignment, not as a persisted drill hierarchy. Sigma's released drill control exposes only id/kind/controlId/controlType and no authorable source, category, or target binding. Retain the first x-axis level, preserve deeper columns, and flag the missing interaction rather than inventing wiring.

ThoughtSpot Answer TML carries per-chart advanced configuration through client_state but has no standalone legend-control artifact. Map recognized chart legend settings to element.legend; do not invent a separate controlType:legend element.
Existing series colors and labels are retained; bar orientation and stacked variants now preserve their source semantics.
Filter controls use controlId as the formula handle and double-nested value sources; element ids remain layout identity only.
Scatter/bubble charts retain their grouped hidden source and groupingId. Source-model joins remain data-model specs and are intentionally unchanged.
ThoughtSpot tabs are top-level dashboard pages, not alternate views sharing one region; mapping them to tabbed-container would change navigation semantics.
Liveboard TML has no documented row-repeating card construct. Do not invent a repeated-container from ordinary tiles.
Liveboard TML has no print-pagination marker. Emitting a Sigma page-break would invent source intent.

Native progress requires trustworthy min/max/value formulas. Current ThoughtSpot TML extraction does not expose a stable gauge range, so GAUGE remains an explicit flagged fallback instead of a misleading progress bar.

ThoughtSpot Liveboard filters are in-canvas controls in this converter; no documented TML header/sidebar panel metadata is available to map. Existing Sigma panel metadata is nevertheless preserved on full-document PUT.
